page_title: How to build a simple actor-based blockchain

sources.entry: Scala: _How to build a simple actor-based blockchain_

summary.title: How to build a simple actor-based blockchain
summary.one_liner: You learn how to model a simple proof-of-work blockchain (Scalachain) in Scala using Akka actors for transactions, mining, persistence and the node API.
keywords: how does proof of work work
takeaways: A blockchain can be modeled as transactions, a linked chain of blocks hashed with SHA-256, and a proof-of-work step that finds a hash with leading zeros.
Scala's sealed traits, case classes and companion objects can represent chain blocks, transactions and messages.
Akka actors split the node into a Broker (pending transactions), a Miner with ready/busy states, a persistent Blockchain actor, and a Node actor that supervises them and exposes a REST API.
Persistent actors store events and snapshots so blockchain state can be recovered after restarts.
summary.summary: This Freecodecamp article walks through Scalachain, a simplified Bitcoin-style blockchain prototype written in Scala. It explains the core model (transactions, chain of hashed blocks, proof of work requiring four leading zeros, and a node exposing a REST API) and then implements each part in code. The actor part uses Akka: a Broker actor manages pending transactions, a Miner actor switches between ready and busy states using become, a PersistentActor stores and recovers the chain, and a Node actor supervises them all. The page ends partway through the Node actor section.
